subject: Post-demo: procurement signal map & budget-owner next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: procurement signal map & budget-owner next steps

Tom — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have one place to track procurement signals and owners heading into your internal procurement meeting next week.

Summary from demo:
- Platform fit: Acme liked predictable latency and dedicated pools for batch pricing.
- Key compliance asks: audit logs and regional isolation (US).

What we need to qualify procurement readiness (ask of Acme):
1) Contracting path: PO + net-30 vs. corporate card (single payment). Do you execute via PO today for SaaS?
2) Marketplace interest: would purchasing via the AWS Marketplace (or Google) simplify procurement approvals?
3) Economic buyer: who signs the business case (title/name)?
4) Finance sponsor: who will own payment & billing discussions (AP contact)?
5) Signatory path: list of approvers and required legal review (any SSO/contractual redlines required?).

Attachments: I’m attaching a lightweight checklist that maps the above to typical approver titles — feel free to mark it up and return. (redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx, Acme_SOW_Draft_v1.pdf)

Proposed next steps:
- Tom / Procurement: confirm PO vs card and whether marketplace would be accepted (due Tue, 21 Jul).
- Acme to share a short approver roster (economic buyer, finance sponsor, legal reviewer).
- We’ll prepare a short SOW + procurement-friendly term sheet once we know the path.

If easier, I can join your procurement sync next Tue to walk the checklist live.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.ai
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@acmeretail.com>, Priya Suresh <priya.s@acmeretail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement signal map & budget-owner next steps

Evelyn — great session yesterday, appreciate the checklist. Quick answers from procurement ops and my side: 

1) Purchase method: Acme prefers PO + net-45 for any multi-month commitments. We rarely use corporate card for platform contracts above $25k ARR.
2) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred when available — simplifies licensing and procurement approvals for our operating regions.
3) Economic buyer: myself (Tom Reynolds), SVP of Digital Ops — will sign the business case but legal may require C-level approval for multi-year deals.
4) Finance sponsor: Priya Suresh (cc’d) — leads AP & vendor onboarding.
5) Signatory path: Procurement Ops (initial review) -> Finance (Priya) -> Legal (TBD: they usually ask for standard SLA/cross-border clauses) -> Me (final business sign-off).

We’ll extract a short approver roster and try to push it across by Tue 21 Jul. Also attaching our internal vendor onboarding template — you can map fields against your checklist.

One constraint: we need to confirm data residency assurances before Legal gives final sign-off.

—
Tom Reynolds
SVP, Digital Operations
Tom.Reynolds@acmeretail.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement signal map & budget-owner next steps

Tom — perfect, that gives us what we need to prepare the right artifacts. Two quick clarifications so we align the SOW & procurement packet: 

A) Marketplace: we can offer an AMI-licensed or marketplace SKU for AWS. Ben, can you confirm commercial differences (pricing & billing flow) vs direct invoice for Acme?
B) Data residency: our hosted US regions and Private (VPC) deployment both keep data in-region; I’ll attach a short note on regional isolation and audit log options for Legal.

Next actions (owner):
- Ben Carter: prepare a short pricing note (marketplace vs invoice) + estimated lead time for vendor onboarding. (Ben)
- Marissa Cole: pull a templated regional-privacy note and examples of audit-log exports for legal. (Marissa)
- Tom / Procurement: share the approver roster and vendor onboarding form by Tue 21 Jul. (Tom)

I’ll stitch these into a procurement packet and send a draft SOW for review by end of week. If helpful, we can do a 20-min procurement-only call next Tue.

Thanks all — Evelyn

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeretail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement signal map & budget-owner next steps

Eve / Marissa / Tom — taking this on. Short note from pricing ops: 

- Marketplace (AWS): billing via AWS Marketplace will be month-to-month at list price with AWS fees. Pros: easier procurement sign-off; Cons: slightly higher unit price and different invoicing cadence.
- Direct invoice (PO/net-45): supports annual commit discounts and reserved capacity pricing (saves ~20% on typical ACME-like usage).

I’ll drop a one-page pricing comparison + vendor onboarding checklist by EOD Thu so you have something to circulate to legal/finance. Marissa — please ping me if you need more detail on feature-enabled SKUs for SOW.

—
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
